newsitem.title: UK: Sterling Eurobond spreads steady on UK budget.
newsitem.headline: Sterling Eurobond spreads steady on UK budget.

text.p: Spreads on sterling Eurobonds were unchanged following the British budget, dealers said on Tuesday.
"We have seen virtually no business, the budget has not had any effect on sterling Eurobonds," said a trader at a major British bank.
"(Chancellor of the Exchequer Kenneth) Clarke presented a tight budget which was pretty much what was expected, and there has been no impact on sterling Eurobonds," he said.
Clarke said the budget contained tax cuts worth 2.0 billion stg, and next year's public spending would be reduced by the same amount.

But expectations of further interest rate rises remained. Fiscal austerity was combined with an over-ambitious inflation target, giving mixed signals which were not enough to calm rate worries, analysts said.
"The budget very much provides a green light for further bonds," said a syndicate head at another British bank.
"With upward pressure still on short-term rates, investors will continue to want to extend along the yield curve."
He said if Wednesday's auction of 2002 gilts went well, European investors might be persuaded to buy Eurobonds at that maturity too.
Sterling's continued strength meant further deals aimed at Japanese investors attracted by both the currency and higher sterling yields were likely to surface, dealers said.
"The same type of issues we have seen recently will continue towards the end of the year, with a few more Japanese-driven issues expected," said a trader.

Further ahead, the government's plans to double the amount of public sector projects financed by the private sector under the Private Finance Initiative (PFI) to 14 billion stg by March 1999 would also increase Eurobond business, dealers said.
